scope: Design-only editable SVG with companion PNG; static flows, not an interactive prototype
basePolicy: 276 base boards include 12 reserved S14 boards showing scoped Settings without any weather entry. Actual S14 lives only in conditional-full. This preserves 23-ID bookkeeping without inventing a hidden-feature entry.

pages.title: source.local_photos.title
pages.externalUI: Application hand-off only. Never draw or counterfeit the system permission dialog. Android Photo Picker availability is runtime-detected; SAF fallback.

pages.title: source.nas.title
pages.gateNote: NAS values are fictional inputs, not verified connections. SMB dependency and security properties remain M0-gated.

platformMeaning.ipad: Android capability note for cross-platform comparison; no iPad dialog is represented
platformMeaning.android: Normal Android path; no invented runtime permission

pages.title: cert.title
pages.gateNote: Illustrative TOFU candidate. Default deny; acknowledgement is not a completed connection. Expired certificates cannot be trusted.

pages.title: cleartext.title
pages.gateNote: Private-cleartext rule is an UNVERIFIED candidate. M0 ATS/networkSecurityConfig, DNS, redirects and resolved-address checks are required. No request was made.

pages.title: weather.title
pages.gateNote: Conditional-full only: M0 weather provider, privacy, attribution, proxy and quota must pass. No entry in scoped navigation. No live weather data.

nativeAcceptance: All screen images are design renders, not running native apps
Android PNG uses local font approximation, not native sans-serif metrics
OS maximal accessibility size, VoiceOver/TalkBack order and touch targets require native acceptance
OS permission sheets, safe-area insets, keyboard avoidance, native material and navigation gestures require real-device tests
NAS/SMB, TOFU and private cleartext are designs only; no M0 success asserted
Google policy/OAuth/retention and weather provider gates remain unpassed
No visual sign-off by user or live-device acceptance
Synthesized landscapes are design samples, not product test fixtures
